correctness.summary: Reduced modular coordinates give SR=1/Im(tau). Hyperbolic circles about the order-three point reduce the fixed-distance problem to exact vertical-coordinate extrema on three boundary pieces; the two branches meet at the square torus and invert algebraically.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: Loewner's bound, conformal-factor variance defects, and the standard 1/Im(tau) modular formula are excluded. No located source states the sharp two-sided modular-distance profile, its exact inverse, or the square-torus phase transition. Material classical-folklore risk remains.

value.summary: The result gives a complete global sharp stability diagram for the flat-torus Loewner/Hermite optimum on the natural modular orbifold, including all equality families and an exact inverse distance bound.

limitations: Only flat two-tori up to similarity are treated.
The modular metric is normalized to curvature -1.
The theorem profiles systolic ratio only, not other shape invariants.
Originality is to the best of our knowledge; equivalent classical reduction-theory folklore may exist.
